correctness.rationale: With Haar probability measure and unnormalized irreducible characters (Haar L2 norm one), use SU(2) multiplicity-one Clebsch–Gordan identity χ_aχ_b=Σ_{j=|a−b|,step2}^{a+b}χ_j. Schur orthogonality makes product-pair overlaps zero for differing sum parity and, for m≥L, exactly m+1+(min(s+t,u+v)−max(|s−t|,|u−v|))/2 otherwise. Expanding the L4 fourth moment produces mF(c)+B_S(c), F=|U²+V²|²+4|UV|² with U and V sum of even and odd coefficients. All correction factors have magnitude at most L+1, and Σ|c_s|≤sqrt(n) on the unit ℓ2-sphere gives |B_S|≤(L+1)n² independent of m. Cauchy bounds |U|²≤ex,|V|²≤o(1−x), relative phase alignment, and Q(x)=e²x²+6eo x(1−x)+o²(1−x)² establish three exact branches including e=3o and o=3e boundary uniqueness. For e,o>0 in strict mixed regime stationary point x=o(3e−o)/(6eo−e²−o²) and C=8e²o²/(6eo−e²−o²), with classwise equal coefficients and relative phase ±. Uniform finite correction plus compactness gives convergence of every unit optimizer to this exact profile set. Independently computed fourth moment by direct fusion 870 and via parity-plus-correction formula 870 for S={0,2,3,5}, m=11, complex coefficients, and exact rational test branch values (1,1):2, (2,1):32/7, (3,1):9, (2,2):8, (4,1):16, (5,0):25. These finite computations check normalization and phase but are not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality PASS for the sharp limit and limiting optimizer classification of moving fixed finite central SU(2) character packets, with universal parity-count dependence and 3:1 boundary. Full primary Travaglini 1982 addresses weighted maximal-torus A_p criteria and single-character uniform norms; full Dooley–Gupta 1996 concerns noncentral matrix coefficients in a single high-weight irreducible. Neither proves the sharp sparse central multi-weight optimization. Classical Clebsch–Gordan decomposition, Schur orthogonality and quadratic optimization are correctly treated as inputs rather than new. No independence/certification claim is made; older character and orthogonal-polynomial literature may overlap.
residual_risks: Older SU(2) central character maximal estimates may encode an equivalent packet asymptotic under Chebyshev or orthogonal-polynomial language.
Search scope finite; self-hit excluded and failure to find is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: A natural small-band spectral optimization problem on a nonabelian compact group. The exact universal answer unexpectedly depends only on even/odd counts, not gaps, and has a sharp 3:1 change between single-parity and mixed extremizers. The piecewise sharp growth constant, uniform O(1) error, and optimizer rigidity yield a substantive theorem connecting representation fusion and geometric optimization, not just a single character norm or routine substitution.

limitations: Only central packet of fixed finite offset set as m→∞; no uniformity when gaps grow, no exact finite-m optimizer.
Classical fusion and Haar normalization are inputs; no noncentral or multiplier conjecture solved.
residual_risks: Older SU(2) central character maximal estimates may encode an equivalent packet asymptotic under Chebyshev or orthogonal-polynomial language.
Search scope finite; self-hit excluded and failure to find is not proof of novelty.
